open_points.subject: platform manifest authority
open_points.text: A microservice exists for the kernel only as a platform-manifest record.
open_points.question: Who supplies and authenticates the manifest, how the kernel observes changes, and whether its contents are trusted configuration or untrusted input?
options: installation-owned trusted manifest
repository-loaded signed manifest
untrusted manifest validated by the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Treat the installation-selected manifest as trusted configuration and re-read it before manifest-sensitive actions.

open_points.subject: operation-node binding reference
open_points.text: An operation node invokes one declared operation of one microservice; only the kernel performs it.
open_points.question: What immutable identifier does an operation node store to select an accepted binding when multiple proposals or accepted replacements exist?
options: binding-version identifier
service and operation name resolved to the latest accepted binding
pinned operation-record digest
open_points.default_guess: Store and pin an accepted binding-version identifier in the flow version.

open_points.subject: schema representation and equality
open_points.text: An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.
open_points.question: What schema language is used, and what exact equality rule determines that two schemas are the same?
options: byte-identical canonical schema documents
structural equality after normalization
equality by immutable schema identifier
open_points.default_guess: Use immutable canonical schema documents and compare their canonical digests.

open_points.subject: digest identities
open_points.text: identified by the digest of the code together with its contract version
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm, serialization and canonicalization define identities for code, values, requests, manifest records and other digested objects?
options: one canonical encoding and digest for every object kind
object-specific canonical encodings with one digest algorithm
opaque store-generated identities plus informational digests
open_points.default_guess: Define an object-specific canonical byte encoding and use one fixed cryptographic digest algorithm.

open_points.subject: contract-version lifecycle
open_points.text: an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract version
open_points.question: When another contract version is authored for an existing slot, what makes a contract version current, and can an older contract version become current again?
options: newly authored version becomes current automatically
an explicit contract-version activation is required
slots have no single current contract version
open_points.default_guess: Make the newest successfully authored contract version current automatically and retain older versions immutably.

open_points.subject: trial-case oracle
open_points.text: Each contract version has a trial corpus
open_points.question: What does a trial case contain, and what exact predicate makes an implementation pass it?
options: inputs and exact expected outputs
inputs plus a schema or property assertion
inputs with an expected success or failure outcome
open_points.default_guess: Store inputs and an exact expected result or expected failure, compared using canonical values.

open_points.subject: try versus admission
open_points.text: try an implementation; admit and activate — kernel, when an implementation is submitted
open_points.question: What distinguishes trying, authoring and submitting an implementation, and does authoring automatically run admission or require a separate submission?
options: authoring is submission and triggers admission automatically
try is a preview and a separate submit action triggers admission
every try performs admission and activation when all cases pass
open_points.default_guess: Store on authoring, permit non-mutating tries, and automatically perform admission once when the implementation is submitted.

open_points.subject: failed admission persistence
open_points.text: Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus; an empty corpus refuses.
open_points.question: Is an implementation that fails admission retained with its evidence and verdict, and can it later be retried after the corpus or implementation changes?
options: retain the implementation and failed verdict
discard the implementation
retain the implementation but not the trial evidence
open_points.default_guess: Retain the immutable implementation, per-case evidence and failed verdict without activating it.

open_points.subject: corpus changes after activation
open_points.text: Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus
open_points.question: What happens to an active implementation when a trial case is later added or captured, so its prior verdict no longer covers the whole current corpus?
options: deactivate it immediately
keep it active but mark its admission stale
automatically re-admit it and deactivate only on failure
open_points.default_guess: Keep it recorded but suspend its activation until automatic re-admission over the enlarged corpus succeeds.

open_points.subject: deterministic sandbox runtime
open_points.text: Admission is a deterministic verdict
open_points.question: Which Python version, standard-library build, platform environment and serialization rules are pinned so that admission and real execution are deterministic and reproducible?
options: installation-pinned runtime image recorded with evidence
one product-defined runtime version
determinism promised only within one running installation
open_points.default_guess: Pin and record a product-defined sandbox runtime image for every execution.

open_points.subject: sandbox resource bounds
open_points.text: bounded time, memory, output and processes
open_points.question: What quantities and units are bounded, where their values come from, and which limit violations produce which observable failure?
options: bounds declared in each contract
installation-wide fixed bounds
contract bounds capped by installation maxima
open_points.default_guess: Use contract-declared bounds capped by installation maxima and report the specific exceeded resource.

open_points.subject: flow external interface
open_points.text: A flow is an immutable, acyclic graph
open_points.question: How are a flow's value inputs and outputs declared and connected, and what values must a caller provide when running it?
options: explicit typed flow input and output ports
source and sink nodes inside the graph
operation nodes are the only sources while terminal edge values are outputs
open_points.default_guess: Give each flow version explicit typed value input and output ports; file ports remain available only through operation nodes.

open_points.subject: map semantics
open_points.text: a map of a node over a collection
open_points.question: What is mapped, whether results preserve order, how per-item failures affect other items and the run, and whether the mapped body may be more than one node?
options: one node mapped sequentially with ordered results
one node mapped concurrently with ordered results
a mapped subgraph with independently traced items
open_points.default_guess: Map exactly one node over elements, preserve input order, trace each execution, and let any item failure fail that map result while independent graph branches continue.

open_points.subject: guard semantics
open_points.text: a guard on a declared closed value
open_points.question: What is the closed value, how branches are declared and selected, whether exhaustiveness is required, and how unselected nodes appear in traces?
options: an exhaustive enum-valued branch selector
a boolean guard with skipped nodes
a tagged union whose cases each select a subgraph
open_points.default_guess: Use an exhaustive declared enum, select one branch, and record other branch nodes as skipped without executing them.

open_points.subject: effect-class authority
open_points.text: Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.
open_points.question: Who assigns an operation's effect class, where it is stored and pinned, and what prevents an agent from understating the class?
options: the platform manifest declares it and the accepted binding pins it
the owner assigns it while accepting a binding
the flow author assigns it and proof validates it
open_points.default_guess: Require the manifest operation record to declare the class and have owner acceptance pin that declaration in the binding.

open_points.subject: draft-write resend authorization
open_points.text: a `draft-write` runs under the owner's activation of the flow instead ... [but] An effect resolved as not applied is sent again only with a fresh approval
open_points.question: How can a draft-write obtain the required fresh approval after `not_applied` when draft-writes do not ordinarily stop for approval?
options: create an `awaiting_approval` step for that resend
require the owner to reactivate the flow
do not apply the fresh-approval rule to draft-writes
open_points.default_guess: Create a one-time exact-request approval step before resending the draft-write.

open_points.subject: standing-approval eligibility
open_points.text: a `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive` node stops ... unless ... a standing approval ...; `destructive` never takes a grant
open_points.question: May standing approvals be granted only to state-transition and external-effect nodes, or also to read and draft-write nodes even though those nodes never ask?
options: only state-transition and external-effect
every class except destructive
all effectful classes including draft-write
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for state-transition and external-effect nodes.

open_points.subject: idempotency key semantics
open_points.text: The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key and never repeats an effect without a fresh approval.
open_points.question: How is the key derived, what attempt or run scope keeps it stable, and whether a post-`not_applied` resend reuses or replaces it?
options: stable per operation-node execution across all resends
new key for every approved send
manifest-declared request field populated from run and node identity
open_points.default_guess: Derive it from run, node and mapped-item identity, place it as declared by the binding, and reuse it for every send of the same logical node execution.

open_points.subject: run completion aggregation
open_points.text: A failed node stops only its dependants.
open_points.question: When independent branches continue after a node fails, what determines when the run ends and whether its terminal status is `failed` or `succeeded` with partial outputs?
options: any failed node makes the eventual run failed
only failure of a required output path makes the run failed
each branch has an outcome and the run may partially succeed
open_points.default_guess: Run all still-runnable independent nodes, then end the run `failed` if any node failed.

open_points.subject: trace values and owner access
open_points.text: input and output by digest ... The owner receives every value ... Values and the records that name them are kept
open_points.question: Do traces expose only digests or permit the owner to retrieve the stored values behind those digests, and through which named action?
options: traces contain digests with a separate owner-only value-read action
owner trace reads expand digests to values
values are returned only as immediate run outputs and are otherwise irretrievable
open_points.default_guess: Keep digests in trace records and add an owner-only read-by-digest operation, subject to secret withholding.

open_points.subject: effect-attempt persistence
open_points.text: inspect ... effect attempts
open_points.question: Are effect attempts distinct immutable records, trace records, or fields on approvals, and which exact request, send and outcome facts do they retain?
options: distinct attempt records linked to traces
one trace record per operation-node attempt
mutable state on the run's operation node
open_points.default_guess: Store each send attempt as a distinct immutable record linked to the node trace, approval and exact request digest.

open_points.subject: business facts versus retained values
open_points.text: It stores no business fact ... [but stores] bounded values that edges carry ... for as long as the kernel keeps its traces; this kernel expires nothing.
open_points.question: What distinguishes a prohibited business fact from a retained edge value that may itself contain business or personal facts?
options: the kernel may retain non-authoritative copies of business values
only digests may be retained after a run
all bounded edge values are exempt from the business-fact exclusion
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the exclusion as prohibiting authoritative business records while allowing immutable execution values retained as trace evidence.

open_points.subject: secret-free traces
open_points.text: Traces carry no secret
open_points.question: Which trace fields and value bodies are inspected or suppressed, how verbatim secrets are recognized across data types, and what happens when safe redaction cannot be established?
options: store only digests for potentially secret-bearing bodies
scan serialized values against configured secret bytes and withhold matches
permit only schemas whose fields have explicit secret annotations
open_points.default_guess: Never place request credentials or raw service bodies in traces; retain only digests for bodies that cannot be proven safe.

open_points.subject: read-trace failure
open_points.text: read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —
open_points.question: What observable result occurs for an unknown trace or run reference, an unauthorized request, or unavailable stored data?
options: typed not-found or unauthorized refusal
empty result
the operation is only a list operation and cannot name an unknown trace
open_points.default_guess: Return a typed refusal with a reason for unknown references or failed authentication.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP operation set
open_points.text: one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel
open_points.question: How do add-trial-case, capture, release, rollback, propose-binding, compose-and-prove and refuse-effect map to this supposedly fixed operation set?
options: they are distinct omitted MCP operations
they are variants of broad `author`, `inspect` and `approve` operations
one generic command operation carries all action variants
open_points.default_guess: Expose distinct typed MCP operations for every primary action and treat the quoted verbs as informal groups.

open_points.subject: activation actor over MCP
open_points.text: the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel
open_points.question: Is `activate` owner-only as this list says, or may an agent invoke it for a proven read-only flow as K-08 and the primary action table say?
options: agents may activate read-only flows and owners may activate any proven flow
only owners invoke activate, while read-only activation is automatic on proof
separate owner and agent activation operations
open_points.default_guess: Permit the same activate operation to agents only for proven read-only versions and to the owner for every proven version.

open_points.subject: agent context delivery
open_points.text: For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies.
open_points.question: Which action requests these repair or composition contexts, what its output schema and failure are, and what qualifies as `recent`?
options: dedicated context operations with a fixed count
variants of inspect with caller-supplied pagination
automatic context attached to author and compose actions
open_points.default_guess: Make them typed inspect variants with deterministic pagination and an installation-defined bounded default window.

open_points.subject: continuation by a second agent
open_points.text: A second agent with the same access continues the work from the kernel's records, the platform manifest and the repositories alone.
open_points.question: What concrete action and observable evidence demonstrate that a second agent can continue, and which required state must be present in each source?
options: an inspection bundle reconstructs all authoring context
ordinary inspect and repository access are sufficient
this is an acceptance scenario rather than a kernel action
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an acceptance scenario requiring ordinary typed inspections to expose every kernel-held dependency by immutable identity.

open_points.subject: function input disclosure ceilings
open_points.text: A binding declares ... the highest class each input accepts ... The flow proof refuses an edge that would deliver a value to an input accepting less.
open_points.question: Where is the highest accepted disclosure class declared for function input ports, so edges into function nodes can be proved?
options: in the function contract for every input port
functions implicitly accept personal_data
the flow version declares a ceiling for each function-node input
open_points.default_guess: Require every function contract input port to declare its maximum accepted class.

open_points.subject: classification of source values
open_points.text: Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data` ... A function's output takes the highest class its execution received.
open_points.question: Who assigns the class of caller-supplied flow inputs, literals, guard values, trial fixtures and zero-input function outputs, and what is the highest class when a function receives no inputs?
options: classes are declared on every source port and literal
all caller and literal values default to open
the submitting actor supplies a class subject to a declared ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Declare a class on every source and literal; make zero-input function outputs `open` unless the contract declares a stricter fixed class.

open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: the highest class
open_points.question: What exact ordering or lattice defines `highest`, including whether all three classes are linearly ordered?
options: open < business_confidential < personal_data
business_confidential and personal_data are incomparable
an explicit policy table rather than an ordering
open_points.default_guess: Use the linear order open < business_confidential < personal_data.

open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: Agents act for the owner with tokens configured in the installation
open_points.question: What authenticates the owner's own requests, where that credential is configured, and how owner requests are distinguished from an agent relaying messages through the same channel?
options: a distinct owner token
host-proxy authenticated owner identity
the agent channel signs owner confirmations separately
open_points.default_guess: Configure a distinct owner token at the installation and authenticate it independently on every request.

open_points.subject: stable agent identity
open_points.text: each agent's ... actions are distinguishable in every record
open_points.question: What stable non-secret agent identifier is associated with a token and recorded, especially after token rotation or removal?
options: configuration-assigned immutable agent ID
digest of the token
caller-supplied agent name
open_points.default_guess: Associate each token with an immutable configuration-assigned agent ID and record that ID, never the token.

open_points.subject: authentication failure behavior
open_points.text: revoking an agent is removing its token, and it takes effect at the agent's next request
open_points.question: What observable failure is returned for missing, unknown, revoked or insufficient-right tokens, and is any attempted actor identity recorded?
options: one authentication refusal with no actor attribution
distinct unauthenticated and forbidden refusals
proxy rejection before the kernel receives the request
open_points.default_guess: Return distinct unauthenticated and forbidden refusals and record only a safe credential identifier when known.

open_points.subject: installation instance changes
open_points.text: An installation selects one manifest instance per service
open_points.question: Can that selection change while flows or runs exist, who changes it, and how a change affects accepted bindings, pinned runs, pending nodes and existing approvals?
options: selection is immutable for the installation lifetime
changes affect new sends and invalidate exact approvals
each run pins the selected instance at start
open_points.default_guess: Allow operational changes; pin the resolved instance per operation attempt, and require a new exact approval whenever the resulting request differs.

open_points.subject: external-send crash boundary
open_points.text: A change is one call in one transaction inside the store module ... outcome handling exist only on operation nodes
open_points.question: What durable state transition occurs before and after an HTTP send so a process crash cannot lose a sent effect or silently repeat it?
options: persist an intent before sending and recover unresolved intents as outcome_unknown
hold the store transaction across the HTTP call
make no guarantee across process crashes
open_points.default_guess: Commit an immutable send intent before I/O and recover any intent lacking a confirmed response as `outcome_unknown`.

open_points.subject: exact replay
open_points.text: Idempotency keys, exact replay and outcome handling exist only on operation nodes
open_points.question: What is replayed exactly, when replay is allowed, and whether exactness covers semantic request fields, canonical bytes or transport framing?
options: the approved logical request fields
the original serialized HTTP bytes
the request excluding transport-generated framing
open_points.default_guess: Replay the approved method, URL, headers and logical body parts, excluding transport-generated multipart boundaries and content length.

open_points.subject: plain-call outcome rule
open_points.text: other operations are plain calls that succeed or refuse
open_points.question: How does this binary rule relate to actions whose declared outcomes include failed trials, failed runs, `awaiting_approval`, `pending`, cancellation and timeout?
options: the rule concerns only synchronous API-call acceptance
all non-operation-node actions must return only success or refusal
long-running domain outcomes are successful call results
open_points.default_guess: Interpret success or refusal as the synchronous command result, with trial evidence and run states represented as successful returned domain records.
